citations.claim: detector_fail on W starts, NS wait 44s, phase EW green
EW still green 90s later, NS wait now 134s exceeding max_green 47
first violation step, NS wait 201s with queue 107 at red, EW still green

counterfactual.change: removed detector_fail event (events: [] instead of W fail). With no failure, max_green is enforced and EW does not lock, so max_wait never violated.

explanation: EW direction green exceeds max_green_seconds 47 and stays green continuously from ~570 to 767 while detector_fail on W is active from 610 onward. Because max_green is not enforced when detector is failed (or the controller thinks no demand / queue invisible interfers with gap-out logic) the EW phase never terminates, so NS approaches wait 201s at red with queues >100, exceeding 200s limit. Removing the detector_fail makes the scenario pass, confirming max_green bypass during detector failure.

violation.detail: approach 0 has waited 201 s at red with vehicles queued (limit 200)

vision_note: Across steps 764 to 767 the NS approaches remain red with large queued backlogs shown by blue dots, while the EW direction stays green (green dots). The red-highlighted violating vehicle remains stopped at the red NS approach for multiple consecutive seconds with no signal change.
